subject: Sizing guidance for dedicated commit — long-context chat + embeddings
messages:
From: Laura Chen <laura.chen@sentinel.ai>
To: Evelyn Hart <evelyn.hart@redwood.com>
Cc: Tom Sloane <tom@novum.ai>, procurement@sentinel.ai
Date: Mon, 12 Oct 2026 09:22:00 -0700
Subject: Dedicated capacity sizing question — long-context chat + embeddings

Hi Evelyn —

Thanks for taking this. Quick background: Sentinel is evaluating a Dedicated capacity commit for Q1. Our workload mix looks roughly like this (daily average):
- 60% interactive chat (short context, 2–8 turns) — target P95 latency <= 300ms
- 30% high-throughput embeddings (batch & realtime) — cost sensitive
- 10% long-context, retrieval-augmented chat (up to ~150k tokens in rare flows) — latency can be softer but not at the cost of OOMs

Traffic profile: ~250M tokens/day, peak ~380 QPS across regions (US primary). We currently run a few open models in-house, quantized to int8 where possible; moving to Redwood Dedicated would be primarily to lower tail latency and get predictable throughput with an SLA.

Two asks:
1) High-level SKU recommendation for Dedicated (H100 vs A100 vs L4) given the mix above — we care about memory headroom for the long-context path and cost per token for embeddings.
2) A suggested pilot allocation (how many of each GPU to reserve) and a short explanation of tradeoffs (memory, throughput, fallback behavior).

Attached: workload_sample.csv (request breakdown by route), SLA_requirements.pdf. Happy to hop on a brief call if that helps.

Thanks,
Laura
Laura Chen
Head of Platform, Sentinel AI

(attachments: workload_sample.csv, SLA_requirements.pdf)

Laura —

Appreciate the detail. I'm looping in Dev (runtime/serving) and Ben (solutions) to give a concise pilot proposal and the tradeoffs. High level answer: you should expect a hybrid dedicated pool. The long-context flows will practically require H100-class memory headroom; embeddings are a great fit for L4-class devices for cost efficiency. A100 sits in the middle and is useful as a fallback and for quantized mid-size models.

Next steps I propose:
- Dev to give a short technical allocation matrix and a rationale (we'll include expected tokens/sec per GPU and concurrency headroom).
- Ben to outline a 30–60 day pilot (reserve counts + pricing delta).
- If that looks good, procurement and Sentinel sign an MSA addendum to lock in reserved SKUs for Q1.

I've attached a quick fitment matrix I ask Dev to populate.

Evelyn

From: Dev Patel <dev_patel@redwood.com>
To: Evelyn Hart <evelyn.hart@redwood.com>, Laura Chen <laura.chen@sentinel.ai>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>, Irene Choi <irene_choi@redwood.com>
Date: Thu, 15 Oct 2026 10:03:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Dedicated capacity sizing question — long-context chat + embeddings

Laura / team —

Below is a concise technical allocation and reasoning based on the workload sample you sent. I included rough performance/cost heuristics so you can see the tradeoffs. Numbers are conservative estimates to give operational headroom.

Summary recommendation (pilot):
- H100 (80GB): 8 cards — primary pool for long-context RAG flows and stateful KV-cache sessions. H100 has the best HBM for very large KV caches and reduced OOM risk for >64k token sessions.
- L4 (48GB inference-class): 10 cards — handle embeddings and high-concurrency, cost-efficient generation for short-chat paths when quantized to int8.
- A100 (40/80GB): 4 cards — intermediate fallback for mid-size models and burst capacity for chat if H100 is saturated.

Why this split?
1) Memory headroom: Long-context sessions consume KV cache proportional to prefix length and batch concurrency. H100 80GB provides ~55–60GB usable for model+kv in our fp16 paths (or ~40–45GB usable when keeping additional caches), whereas A100 40GB variants often hit limits for >64k contexts and require more aggressive tiling. That increases latency and engineering complexity.

2) Throughput & cost: L4 is excellent for embeddings — int8 quantization yields 3–5x cost reduction per token vs fp16 / H100 paths. For short chat (low context), L4 can serve many concurrent small sessions with low token cost. H100 provides higher per-card throughput on large-context runs but at higher $/hour.

Estimated operational metrics (pilot, rough):
- H100 80GB: ~450–700 tokens/sec sustained per card for long-context generator models (depending on model size / kv locality).
- A100 80GB: ~350–550 tokens/sec for equivalent fp16 runs; 40GB A100 needs tiling for very long contexts which lowers effective tokens/sec by ~20–30% when tiling is active.
- L4 48GB: ~2k–6k tokens/sec for small-context int8 runs and embeddings throughput in the 10k+ vectors/sec range for batched workloads (depends on vector dim and batch size).

Headroom & concurrency guidance:
- Plan for ~30% headroom on H100 pool for KV cache warmup and spikes (8 cards -> operational concurrency for long-context of ~80–120 active large sessions depending on model).
- For embeddings, L4 pool should be sized for peak batch windows; 10 L4 cards gives you good parallelism for both realtime and batch embedding jobs with room to burst.

Routing & fallback policy (practical):
- Route by route-tag + context_length: if context > 32k tokens -> prefer H100. If context between 8k–32k -> prefer A100 (80GB) when cost sensitivity slightly higher. Else (short) -> L4.
- If preferred pool is saturated, automatically fallback to A100 (if coming from H100) or H100 (if overflow from L4 and model variant requires higher accuracy) with degraded cost/latency SLOs documented in the route config.

Cost tradeoff note (high-level):
- Expect H100 to be ~2.5–3x the $/hour of L4 for equivalent model footprint; A100 sits in the middle. For your workload mix the blended cost delta vs an L4-only approach is justified by the avoidance of OOMs and complexity on long-context flows.

Operational checklist for pilot:
- Pre-warm KV caches for top 10% retrieval flows.
- Enable continuous caching and LRU eviction policy tuned to sessions with >64k contexts.
- Quantize embedding models to int8 for L4; keep generation models in fp16 on H100 when long-context fidelity matters.
- Instrument per-route token and latency telemetry; create regression alerts for P95 latency and OOMs.

Attachments: I ran microbenchmarks on a representative model in our infra — see gpu_microbench_results.csv for tokens/sec baselines I referenced.

Happy to walk through the numbers on a call and adjust allocation if you share model sizes or a sample of the long-context query lengths.

- Dev

Senior Software Engineer, Serving Runtime — Redwood Inference

Subject: Re: Dedicated capacity sizing question — long-context chat + embeddings

Laura / team —

Thanks — the technical allocation looks good and aligned with what we've seen on similar deals. Proposed commercial next steps:
1) 30-day pilot (Nov) with the split Dev recommended: 8x H100, 10x L4, 4x A100. We price the pilot at our standard pilot hourly with a credit toward the committed contract if Sentinel signs by Jan 15.
2) Prepare a Mutual Action Plan (MAP) clarifying deliverables: infra handoff, telemetry dashboard access, joint perf validation, and PO/MSA timeline.
3) Procurement: if you're comfortable we can provision capacity as soon as the MAP is signed; the pilot is non-binding for the final commit numbers.

Evelyn / Dev: can you confirm we have a short MAP draft by Friday? Laura — I can run a quick commercial call Friday or early next week to walk through pricing and options for reserve duration (6/12/24 months).

Ben
Ben Carter
Senior Solutions Engineer — Redwood Inference
